messages.content: What does the SZL thesis say about Abstract?

Per the canonical thesis (v8), section 'Abstract': We report   three machine-checked Lean 4 theorems   that together constitute the formally verified core of the SZL Holdings governed-AI kernel, and we frame them within a cross-disciplinary methodology adapted — never reclaimed — from five established research lineages. Result I    Wave24,  Lutar/QuantumBio/CoherenceDecay.lean   establishes that the  -norm coherence of a single qubit under pure-dephasing Lindblad/GKSL dynamics, modeled as  , is strictly antitone, non-negative, equal to   at  , decays to zero as  , and that the engineering gate value   crosses any closure floor   at a unique finite time  . Result II    Wave25,  Lutar/Lambda/AggregatorLfp.lean   gives a   constructive   Kleene iterate-supremum treatment of the Λ-aggregator least fixed point on a complete lattice: the iterate chain   is monotone, bounded above by  , and the exact Kleene equality   holds   under an explicit ω-continuity commute hypothesis     lfp_eq_iSup_iterate_of_commute  . Result III    Wave26, same file, additive  is the   unconditional   strengthening:  lfp_eq_iSup_iterate    drops   Wave25's explicit hypothesis by  deriving  the commute property from ω-Scott-continuity, using the Mathlib v4.18.0 ωCPO continuity API. What is new in this paper is neither new physics nor new pure mathematics; it is the machine-checked formalization of these classical results in Lean 4 together with their governance application   — a coherence closure-gate single-crossing certificate and a PURIQ router convergence certificate. All three theorems are    VERIFIED    at the EXPERIMENTAL / CI-green tier and merged to  main . Epistemic labels in the source are preserved; nothing here is promoted beyond what the thesis states.

messages.content: Explain 1.1 The thesis: a governed-AI kernel with a verified core in the SZL governed-AI kernel.

Per the canonical thesis (v8), section '1.1 The thesis: a governed-AI kernel with a verified core': This paper presents the formally verified core of the SZL Holdings governed-AI kernel and situates it within a cross-disciplinary methodology. The kernel is the substrate by which an autonomous-system governance decision is treated, at its mathematical center, as a  constrained optimization under honest uncertainty : constraints are stated explicitly and never disguised as theorems, the objective is the correct objective for the resource structure, and every claim carries a precisely labeled epistemic status. The verified core of that kernel is now   three machine-checked Lean 4 theorems  , each of which has passed  lake build  with no  sorry  and with an axiom footprint confined to the Lean-core kernel set  , and each of which is merged to  main  on  szl-holdings/lutar-lean . The three theorems formalize, in the same proof assistant and under the same honesty doctrine, the two characteristic monotone dynamics the kernel's runtime gate and router actually rely on, plus the strengthening that removes a hypothesis from the second:

-   Result I  Wave24    is a  dynamical  result for the SZL Λ-v5 coherence gate. The locked-proven kernel already contains  static  gate lemmas  a decohered node never closes; a discharged node never closes; the gate is monotone in coherence and in charge . Result I supplies the time-dynamics those statics never touched: under pure-dephasing Lindblad dynamics the coherence   is strictly decreasing, decays to zero, and the gate value crosses any closure floor at a unique finite time  . It remains a   convergence   result — the constructive computation of the lfp — and is explicitly   not   a uniqueness claim, so it does not bear on Conjecture 1. messages.content: Summarize Defect 1 — The no-equivocation assumption is aimed at the wrong party for the governed estate.

Per the estate doctrine (research/CONJECTURE2-PLAN-CORRECTIONS.md), section 'Defect 1 — The no-equivocation assumption is aimed at the wrong party': Plan text  defective :   the no-equivocation assumption is stated over
 corrupt authors  — a byzantine validator does not sign two conflicting
blocks. That is an assumption about adversary behavior, which a safety proof
cannot demand: equivocation is precisely what byzantine actors do. Counterexample shape:   let validator  v  be corrupt and sign both
 B_r^x   round  r , slot  x   and  B_r^y   round  r , slot  y ≠ x  . Under the
plan's assumption this is excluded by fiat, so the safety proof is vacuous for
the byzantine case it exists to cover. No quorum-intersection argument can
recover, because the intersection guarantee  "at least one honest witness" 
only constrains  honest  voters. This is the standard byzantine-quorum
shape and matches the Wave23 lemma's actual content.
